extracted.intended_audience: freelance journalists and PR professionals pitching story ideas to Wired
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting and submitting story pitches to Wired, including what kinds of stories the magazine prefers, pitch structure, editorial standards, and submission process expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories about technology's impact on culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories about technology's impact on culture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wired favors pieces that explore how technology shapes cultural life rather than just product details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations into power dynamics in tech
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations into power dynamics in tech
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep reporting that uncovers power relationships, influence, and structural issues within the tech sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form profiles of consequential figures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-depth profiles focused on people who matter to tech and its cultural impact; suitable for long-form feature treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science stories with technical depth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science reporting should include technical rigor and sufficient detail to satisfy expert readers while remaining accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate-tech with verifiable progress
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage of climate technology should demonstrate measurable, verifiable advances rather than speculative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future-oriented pieces with present-day grounding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Futures or trend pieces should be anchored in current developments and evidence, not pure speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid routine product launches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wired does not want routine product-launch coverage; pitches should show a larger story or significance beyond the launch itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid funding announcements without bigger story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple funding news is not sufficient unless tied to a broader trend, impact, or exclusive insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vanity company milestones
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milestone announcements that serve corporate PR without broader relevance are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic 'AI is the future' pieces
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overbroad or generic AI optimism without a specific angle, evidence, or reporting is not wanted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hype without verification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be verifiable; pitches based on unverified hype are weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: specific story angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the subject line to convey a clear, specific angle rather than a vague or generic headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 1: The story angle (1-2 sentences)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a concise statement of the story's central idea—keep it to one or two sentences to make the pitch immediately clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 2: Why now (timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the timeliness or news hook that makes the story relevant at this moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 3: Sources and access available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the sources you can interview and any documents or exclusive access you have; demonstrate reporting feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 4: Why you / why this source
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 4: Why you / why this source
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain your qualifications, prior reporting, or unique access that make you the right person to write this story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive access to people or documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive access to people or documents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive interviews, internal documents, or other unique material strengthen a pitch and can justify coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable data with methodology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data and disclose methodology so editors can assess credibility; methodological transparency is a strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple expert sources arrayed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing a range of knowledgeable sources indicates rigorous reporting and corroboration for major claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual storytelling potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches that lend themselves to strong visuals (photos, graphics, video) are more attractive; list available assets if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection to broader trend
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the specific story to larger patterns or trends to show relevance and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story has been covered elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the topic is already widely covered, the pitch is weaker unless you bring new reporting or a fresh angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single source on a controversial claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Single source on a controversial claim
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying on one source for a controversial assertion undermines credibility; multiple corroborating sources are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous sources without justification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous sourcing must be justified; unexplained anonymous claims weaken a pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual story without visual assets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitching a visually driven piece without offering assets or a plan for visuals is less compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tech-bro framing without consumer impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid industry-insider, promotional framing that doesn't show real-world consequences for people or culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sources for major claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial standard: corroborate important claims with more than one source to meet Wired's verification bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology disclosed for data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting data, disclose how it was collected and analyzed so editors and readers can assess validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest declared
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare any potential conflicts so editors can evaluate bias or competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes verified with sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm attributions and quotations with sources as part of standard editorial verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of reply offered to subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Right of reply offered to subjects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer interviewed subjects a chance to respond before publication as part of fair reporting practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch via specific section editor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send pitches to the correct section editor rather than a generic inbox to improve chances of a timely response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wait two weeks before following up
rubrics_metrics.description: Wait 2 weeks for response before following up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors ask that you wait about two weeks before sending a follow-up query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit to one follow-up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send multiple follow-ups; limit to a single polite follow-up if you haven't heard back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for a 30-minute call
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to discuss the pitch on a short call and to answer questions about access, sources, and framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be available for back-and-forth on framing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may request adjustments to angle or framing; be prepared to collaborate on how the story is positioned.
